correctness.rationale: The cube Morse complex is exhaustively reconstructed from its 24 primitive vector fields. The package verifies 23,624 nonempty faces, an independent rooted-forest face count, a complete acyclic matching with critical counts 1 in degree 0, 44 in degree 5, and 179 in degree 6, and the complete Hasse-orientation acyclicity. The signed algebraic-Morse boundary from degree 6 to degree 5 has exact rank 40 and a determinant-one 40-by-40 minor, so its nonzero Smith factors are units. With no intermediate critical cells, the 5-skeleton is a wedge of forty-four 5-spheres; Hurewicz identifies pi_5 with H_5, so Smith reduction of the attaching matrix gives exactly four surviving 5-spheres and 139 trivially attached 6-spheres.

value.rationale: Hypercubes are explicitly used as a natural test family in the general Morse-complex connectivity literature, and Q_3 is the first hypercube beyond the cycle Q_2. The known exact result for Q_3 stops at mod-2 homology. Determining a full mixed-dimensional sphere wedge resolves integral torsion and all 6-cell attachment ambiguity, giving a structurally stronger and reusable benchmark rather than a routine coefficient check.
